summary.text: General relativity is Einstein's geometric theory of gravity, published in May 1916, which describes gravity as a property of four-dimensional spacetime.
The curvature of spacetime is tied to the energy, momentum and stress of whatever is present, so matter tells spacetime how to curve and spacetime tells matter how to move.
It predicts gravitational time dilation, gravitational lensing, black holes and gravitational waves, and so far every test has agreed with it.

items.prompt: In general relativity, why does the Earth keep circling the Sun?

options.label: The Sun's mass curves spacetime and Earth moves along that curvature
An invisible rope pulls Earth toward the Sun
Earth's motion cancels the Sun's weight exactly
Space around the Sun stays flat and still

items.explain: Mass curves spacetime, and bodies then move according to that curvature.

items.prompt: If general relativity is right, how does Newton's old law of gravity fit with it?

options.label: Newton's law is simply wrong everywhere
The two apply to separate kinds of matter
Newton's law is a good prediction where spacetime is almost flat
Newton's law only works for light

items.explain: Newton's law can be seen as a prediction of general relativity for nearly flat spacetime around stationary masses.

items.prompt: Einstein once added a cosmological constant to his equations. What was his reason at the time?

options.label: To make the universe expand quickly
To fit the common belief that the universe was static
To remove black holes from the theory
To account for Mercury's orbit

items.explain: In line with contemporary thinking he assumed a static universe, and he later called the constant his biggest blunder.

items.prompt: Astronomers saw Mercury's orbit drift in a way Newton's theory could not explain. What did general relativity manage to do about it?

options.label: Explain it without arbitrary fudge factors
Show that a hidden planet must be pulling on it
Explain it by assuming the Sun is not round
Declare the observations to be mistaken

items.explain: Einstein showed in 1915 that his theory explained Mercury's anomalous perihelion advance with no arbitrary parameters.

items.prompt: A physicist describes a region where space and time are distorted so much that not even light can get out. What does the theory call it?

options.label: A gravitational wave
A cosmic background
A neutron field
A black hole

items.explain: Black holes are regions where space and time are distorted so that nothing, not even light, can escape.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to merge general relativity with quantum physics into one theory. What obstacle stands in the way?

options.label: Gravity cannot be measured at small scales
Quantum physics has been proven false
No self-consistent theory of quantum gravity has been found
General relativity has failed every test

items.explain: Reconciling it with quantum physics remains a problem, since no self-consistent theory of quantum gravity has been found.
